    Integer mesh weights and their restriction to rays (Lemma 7.4) #

    weights-and-parameters.tex (def:integer-weights, lem:integer-weight-lifting). An integer mesh weight assigns w(a) to arrows and ν_v to mesh rows with w(σa) + w(a) = ν_v; it restricts to an integer ray weight, and "this restriction gives an exact sequence 0 → {ζ : ζ_P = 0} → H^mesh → H → 0".

    The proof works on the lifted complex. "Pull a ray weight h back to L. By Proposition 7.2, write h(r : x → y) = b_y − b_x […] Choose one lift of each nonprojective label and assign it any integer. Extend by ζ_{gX} = ζ_X + γ(g). Differences along arrows and translation edges are deck invariant, hence descend to a mesh weight."

    Formalization. The deck group of the formalization is the fundamental group of the coned complex, so we work in the component K₀ of a base vertex in the lifted Auslander–Reiten quiver (aconn), whose stabilizer plays the role of the paper's G = π₁(K). The connectivity of the lifted projective category used by the paper is replaced by the support lemma (supp_conn): the lifted projectives with nonzero maps to one lifted object are connected in L, by Lemma 4.8 and the locality of degree-one endomorphisms; hence the lifted projectives of K₀ lie in one component of L (conn_of_aconn).
